questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

I asked the shopkeeper, "What is the price of this bike?"

options.text: I asked the shopkeeper what is the price of this bike.
I asked the shopkeeper that what the price of this bike was.
I asked the shopkeeper what the price of that bike was.
I asked the shopkeeper what was the price of that bike.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3) i.e. I asked the shopkeeper what the price of that bike was.**

 
• The reporting speech in the given sentence is in the **past tense**, hence, while changing it into indirect speech the whole sentence will be in the past sentence.
 
• ‘Wh’ – Question (beginning with – who / what / how / where / when / why, etc.) then before the Reported Speech i.e., Interrogative word, there

 will be no usage of any Conjunction.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. 

A. In a small town in England, there lived a poor little girl.

B. She was very excited but her right shoe was worn out.

C. So, she went to a cobbler to get it mended.

D. Her friend invited her to come to her birthday party.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) ADBC.**

 
• The only **independent** sentence from the given sentences is sentence **'A'**, hence, it will be the first sentence.
 
• In the sentence 'D' the pronoun **'her' ** has been been used for the little girl. This sentence is most suitable for using after sentence 'A'.
 
• The sentence 'D' talks about a **birthday party** and the sentence 'B' the excitement of the girl, hence, we can say that the girl is excited about the birthday party. So, the sentence 'B' will follow the sentence 'D'.
 
• So, we have got the sequence i.e. ADB, hence, the last sentence will be 'C'.

questions.question:
**Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.**

That which cannot be taken by force
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**impregnable**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Impregnable**" is an adjective that describes something so strong or well-constructed that it cannot be taken by force or broken into.

 
 
• This definition directly aligns with the given phrase "that which cannot be taken by force".
 
 
 
• For instance, in the sentence, "*The fortress was **impregnable**, resisting all attempts at invasion,"* the word "**impregnable**" illustrates a structure that can't be conquered or taken by force.
 
• **Synonyms **of "impregnable" include** "invincible", "unassailable", "invulnerable", and "indestructible".**
 
• Hence, the correct answer will be **Option 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: "**Immutable**" means unchanging over time or unable to be changed. It's typically used to describe abstract concepts rather than physical objects.

 
 
• For example:* "The laws of physics are immutable*."
 
• This doesn't fit with the original phrase, as something can be immutable but still be taken by force.
 
 
 
• Option 2: "Inapprehensible" means not able to be understood or comprehended. It's often used to describe complex ideas or abstractions.
 
 
• **For example**: "The philosophy lecture was inapprehensible to most of the students."
 
• This also doesn't fit with the original phrase, as it pertains more to understanding than physical force.
 
 
 
• Option 4: "Inaccessible" describes something that cannot be reached, accessed, or easily obtained.
 
 
• **For example**: "The remote island was inaccessible due to rough seas."
 
• While this could imply a kind of protection, it doesn't necessarily mean that the thing or place can't be taken by force. It simply might be difficult to get to it.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

I try to avoid __travel in__ the rush hour.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• **Rule: A verb can be followed by another verb. The second one usually needs to change into the -ing form or the to + infinitive form. Which form you need depends on what the first verb is. There are certain verbs, when they are followed by another verb, it must be in the -ing form**. 
 
• In the given sentence there are two verbs 'avoid & travel', the verb 'avoid' follows another verb with -ing form, therefore, 'travel' must be replaced by 'travelling'.
 
• The correct preposition to be used is 'in' which is used to mention the unspecific times.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sentence is 'I try to avoid travelling in__ the rush hour.'**

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. 

Bill Gates has given away twenty seven percent of his wealth in charity.

options.text: Twenty seven percent of his wealth has been given away by Bill Gates in charity.
Twenty seven percent of his wealth had been given away by Bill Gates in charity.
Bill Gates has been given away by twenty seven percent of his wealth in charity.
Twenty seven percent of his wealth has given away Bill Gates in charity.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• While changing a sentence to its passive form, subject and object interchange their places.
 
• **The given sentence is in the present perfect tense, so the passive form of this sentence will follow a structure of 'has+been+V3'.tr**
 
• **Therefore,** the structure is followed correctly only by option 1** 'Twenty seven percent of his wealth has been given away by Bill Gates in charity.' **

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order**. 

A. Early on Christmas morning, Pip returns to the graveyard with the ﬁle, a pie, and brandy.

B. On Christmas Eve, Pip, an orphan who is about seven years old, encounters an escaped convict in the village graveyard.

C. The convict scares Pip into stealing food and a ﬁle.

D. Pip, who lives with his elder sister and her husband Joe Gargery, a blacksmith, steals a ﬁle and some food.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is Option 4.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The correct answer begins with sentence B because it is introducing a subject called 'pip'.
 
• In sentence B it is said Pip encountered an escaped convict which is continued in sentence C about what the convict scares him to do.
 
• The sentences describe how Pip meets the convict, gets threatened by him, steals the items, and returns to the graveyard. 
 
• The other options do not make sense as they mix up the sequence of actions.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sequence is followed in Option 4 'BCDA'. **
